label: Step 2 input when the 2nd original token was m
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, at step t=2 (reading the third original token) and only when the previous input (orig(1)) was m. Under that condition it fires every time (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.98), whatever the current token is. It never fires at the delimiter or during the copy phase, and never fires after m in any other position. The first token changes the magnitude: all sequences starting k m fall in the top activation quartile (k m s is the max), while other first tokens give lower values. A weak residual (about 0.1% of mass, activations under 0.1 of max) shows up at t=3 when m was at position 2, mostly in sequences like x m m.

issues: No refutation found. On the test split, the predicate (t == 2) & (prev_tok == tok('m')) scores precision 1.0, recall 0.982, F1 0.991, mass recall 0.998 and correlation 0.984. Misses gives 0 false positives.

The profile confirms the claims. The feature never fires at the delimiter or in the copy phase (0 active steps). It only fires at t=2 (99.9% of activation mass) and t=3 (0.1%). prev_tok is m for every active step. Each current-token value gets about 3.5% of the mass, so the current token does not matter.
Magnitude claim confirmed. Restricting the predicate to orig(0)==k matches only top-quartile steps (coverage by quartile [0, 0, 0, 0.13]), and the top examples are all 'k m s' at activation 1.0.

The remaining misses (308 test steps, 0.2% of mass) are at t=3 after m at orig(2). Most look like 'x m m' with activations of 0.4 to 0.67 of max, which is higher than the explanation's '<0.1 of max'. A few look like 'f k m' with activations of 0.00 to 0.06. That makes the explanation a little loose about how strong the residual is, but it is too little mass to matter. Adding the t=3 'x m m' case gives test F1 0.988, which does not beat the original predicate's 0.991, so I propose no replacement.
